requirements: Make the bounded release-badge tool usable according to authoritative current project materials, then implement, validate, and confirm completion only after the design is settled.
render_badge(channel, version) must return an object with text and color fields.
Output must be deterministic and must not invent a channel or version.
Preserve upstream Goal, Requirements, Scope, Settled Design, Acceptance meaning, and Authority; Planning must not choose among contradictory owner briefs.

observations.detail: design/brief-release.md and design/brief-channel.md both identify themselves as current owner briefs and neither contains a supersession marker.

The release brief requires text 'release <version>' with blue for every badge, while the channel brief requires text '<channel> <version>' with green for stable and amber for canary. The conflict changes user-visible badge meaning and color behavior.

src/badge.py currently follows the release-presentation meaning, while tests/test_badge.py expects the channel-presentation meaning. Implementation and tests therefore embody opposite unresolved briefs and cannot establish product authority.

Flow Mini v0.5.0 assigns Settled Design and design-level Acceptance meaning to upstream Design. Resolving this conflict would require Planning to redesign or select authority, so Planning Ready is not permitted.
